denial.label: Pre-existing disease waiting period not completed

grounds: Idiopathic atrophic hypothyroidism was first diagnosed on 2023-12-26, AFTER the policy start date 2023-07-03; by definition it is not a Pre-Existing Disease, so the waiting period does not apply.
letter:
Subject: Appeal against Denial D03 – Pre‑existing disease waiting period not completed (Claim ID a2fb233f-60e0-b477-ede2-923db6354187)

Claim Details:
- Claim ID: a2fb233f-60e0-b477-ede2-923db6354187
- Patient ID: a2fb233f-60e0-b477-cd38-af3923f792a3
- Patient Name: Tanner Amos Mitchell
- Date of Service: 2023‑12‑26
- Policy: Suraksha Silver Individual Health Plan (Plan Code SGH‑SILVER)
- Coverage Start Date: 2023‑07‑03
- Diagnosis: Idiopathic atrophic hypothyroidism
- Total Claim Amount: INR 342.2

Grounds for Appeal:
The diagnosis of idiopathic atrophic hypothyroidism was first made on 26 December 2023, which is after the policy start date of 3 July 2023. According to the policy definition, a condition first diagnosed on or after the policy start date is not a Pre‑Existing Disease and therefore is excluded from the waiting period provision [suraksha_silver_policy#5]. Consequently, the 36‑month Pre‑Existing Disease waiting period stipulated in Clause 4.2 does not apply to this claim [suraksha_silver_policy#11].

The insurer bears the burden of proving that an exclusion or waiting period is applicable. In this case, no documentary evidence has been provided to demonstrate that the condition existed prior to the policy start date, as required by the denial standards [claims_procedure_and_grievance#6]. The denial therefore fails to meet the insurer’s evidentiary obligation.

Clinical Necessity:
The treating physician will attach detailed clinical notes confirming that the treatment for idiopathic atrophic hypothyroidism was medically necessary and was initiated promptly after diagnosis.

Reference to Denial Standards:
The appeal is made in accordance with the insurer’s grievance procedure, which allows the provider to contest a denial in writing within 30 days, specifying the claim, denial reason, relevant policy clauses, and supporting clinical evidence [claims_procedure_and_grievance#8].

Specific Request:
In view of the above, we respectfully request that the denial be withdrawn, the claim be re‑processed, and the amount of INR 342.2 be paid in full.

Thank you for your prompt attention to this matter.

Insurance Desk (on behalf of the treating provider)

citations.section: Suraksha Silver Individual Health Plan (Policy Wording) > 4. Waiting Periods > 4.2 Pre-Existing Disease Waiting Period
citations.quote:
### 4.2 Pre-Existing Disease Waiting Period
Expenses related to a Pre-Existing Disease (as defined in Clause 2.2) are covered only after 36 months of continuous coverage from the first policy start date. This waiting period applies ONLY to conditions meeting the definition in Clause 2.2.

citations.section: Claims Procedure, Denial Standards and Grievance Redressal > C3. Standards for Denial > C3.2 Burden of Proof for Exclusions and Waiting Periods
citations.quote:
### C3.2 Burden of Proof for Exclusions and Waiting Periods
The insurer bears the burden of proving that an exclusion or waiting period applies. For a Pre-Existing Disease denial, the insurer must show documentary evidence that the condition was diagnosed or treated before the policy start date.

citations.section: Claims Procedure, Denial Standards and Grievance Redressal > C4. Appeals and Grievances > C4.1 Right to Appeal
citations.quote:
## C4. Appeals and Grievances  
### C4.1 Right to Appeal
The insured, or the provider on the insured's behalf, may appeal a denial in writing within 30 days of the denial letter. The appeal should identify the claim, the denial reason, the policy clauses relied upon and the supporting clinical evidence.
